meta.title: Lease Loop – circular leasing
meta.description: Lease an e-bike, laptop or farm machine. When the lease ends, it gets a second life.
brand.name: Lease Loop
brand.tagline: Circular leasing for e-bikes, laptops and farm machines
catalogue.title: Catalogue
catalogue.intro: Every item can be leased, returned, refurbished and leased again.

home.title: Welcome to Lease Loop
home.intro: Lease an e-bike, a laptop or a farm machine for a fixed monthly price. When the lease ends, buy it, return it or pass it on, and the item gets a second life with someone new.
home.catalogueText: Browse the catalogue, pick a term and a down payment, and see your monthly price straight away, explained line by line.
home.fleetText: For companies: pick {min} to {max} items of one kind, answer the questions once and sign once for all of them.
home.step1: Choose an item and see what it costs a month, and why.
home.step2: Answer only the questions that apply to you, and sign online.
home.step3: Pay monthly. When the lease ends, buy the item, return it or pass it on.
home.step4: Returned items are checked, refurbished and leased again.

admin.title: Admin
admin.intro: A control room for demonstrations, on the app’s date ({date}): totals, VAT changes, every contract and the audit log.
admin.items: Items: {available} available · {leased} leased · {reserved} reserved · {returned} returned · {sold} sold.
admin.vat.title: VAT rates
admin.vat.rules: A change applies from its date until the next one, on every invoice, quote and contract. It must start after the app’s date, because tax already charged is not rewritten: time-travel back first to add one earlier. Changes are stored in the database; data/vat-rates.json is never edited, and npm run db:reset brings the original rates back.
admin.vat.errorPast: A VAT change must start after the app’s date.
admin.vat.errorRate: The rate must be between 0 and 100 %, with at most two decimals.
admin.vat.errorInForce: This VAT change has already started, so it can’t be removed.
admin.vat.errorGeneric: That didn’t work. Please try again.
admin.auditNote: Every change (applications, signatures, returns, payments, VAT) is written here in the same transaction as the change itself.

exit.title: End the lease early
exit.intro: You can end the lease before its last day: buy the item now, or return it now. Here is exactly how the price is worked out.
exit.marketValue: What the item is worth today
exit.explained: Paying now instead of later saves the interest, so each future rent and the buyout are discounted back to today at the monthly interest rate. If you return the item, its value today is taken off what you still owe.
exit.buyText: {net} + {vat} VAT. The item is yours and the lease ends today.
exit.returnText: {net} + {vat} VAT: what you still owe, minus what the item is worth today.
exit.coolingOff: Free: you are still in the first month of the lease, so you can return it without a fee.

co2.title: Circular impact
co2.firstLife: Life {lives} of this item. Reuse savings start when it is leased again after its first life.
co2.reused: Life {lives} of this item: {reuse} time(s) someone leased it instead of a new one being made.
co2.ridingSaved: CO₂ saved by riding, not driving
co2.howPerLife: Making a new one causes {newKg} kg CO₂e. Refurbishing costs 12 % of that, so a reuse life avoids up to {perLife} kg.
co2.howLifeLeft: An almost worn-out item replaces only part of a new one, so the saving is scaled by the life it has left: {percent} % (its age, condition and usage, the same factors that set its price). Money saved uses the same share.
co2.howToday: We only know the item as it is today, so every reuse life uses today’s share. Earlier lives were in better shape, so this under-counts rather than over-claims.
co2.howRiding: Riding counts every km as a car trip avoided (0.15 kg/km). It would happen with a new bike too, so it is shown apart from the reuse saving. All factors are fictional.
co2.fleetDetail: {items} item(s) have been reused, {lives} reuse life/lives in total.
